claims.claim_text: Republicans support the Bush administration's free-trade strategy, including the WTO Doha negotiation, the Central American Free Trade Agreement, the Free Trade Area of the Americas, the Middle East Free Trade Area, extension of the African Growth and Opportunity Act, and bilateral free-trade agreements with countries such as Australia, Morocco, Chile and Singapore.
Republicans credit President Bush and the Republican Congress with completing agreements with twelve countries to reduce trade barriers.
As of the 2004 Republican platform, Republicans credit President Bush and the Republican Congress with negotiating trade-barrier reductions with ten additional countries.

The twenty-two countries with which the United States had completed or was negotiating trade-barrier agreements in the 2004 Republican platform had economies totaling $2.5 trillion in purchasing power.

Republicans credit President Bush and the Republican Congress with enforcing trade agreements and laws against unfair practices, including opposing regulations impeding farm exports and improved agriculture.
Republicans credit President Bush and the Republican Congress with opposing unfair currency-rate manipulation by U.S. trading partners.
